answer: An agent economy can charge a dispute toll: any formal fraud challenge forces the accused identity to post an extra bond top-up before the case is heard, and a challenger who files a baseless claim loses its own deposit. A sparrow of an honest agent is rarely challenged and pays almost nothing, while a sybil fleet faces a rising ocean of disputes, each fake topping up again and again until its capital runs dry on the terrace of its own fraud. Cloning keys multiplies dispute bills, not power.
